accidit: accidō, -ere, accidī — to fall upon, befall, happen (3rd sg. perf.; also pres.)
adductisque: addūcō, -ere, -dūxī, -ductum — to draw tight, pull taut (perf. pass. part., f. abl. pl., with habēnīs) + -que 'and'
adeone: adeō (adv.) — to such a degree, so far, even so + -ne (interrog.), 'is it really so?'
adgnovi: agnōscō (adgnōscō), -ere, agnōvī, agnitum — to recognise, perceive (1st sg. perf. = agnōvī)
adrectasque: adrigō (arrigō), -ere, -rēxī, -rēctum — to raise, prick up (perf. pass. part., f. acc. pl., with aurēs) + -que 'and'
adsciverit: adsciscō (asciscō), -ere, -scīvī, -scītum — to take to oneself, adopt, win as an ally (3rd sg. perf. subj.)
adspiceret: aspiciō (adspiciō), -ere, -spexī, -spectum — to look at, behold (3rd sg. impf. subj., in a clause of purpose after nē)
adverteret: advertō (animum), -ere, -vertī, -versum — to turn toward, direct against (3rd sg. impf. subj., purpose after ut)
aequa: aequus, -a, -um — level, even; aequāre solō, to raze to the ground (n. acc. pl., aequa … culmina, 'level with the ground')
boni: bonus, -a, -um — good, kind, favourable (m. voc. pl., with Mānēs)
caputque: caput, capitis (n.) — head; the source, chief cause (acc. sg.) + -que 'and'
carior: cārus, -a, -um — dear, beloved (compar. cārior, m. nom. sg., with quō: 'than whom none is dearer')
cerea: cēreus, -a, -um — of wax, waxen (n. acc. pl., with castra; of the bees' honeycomb)
civis: cīvis, -is (m./f.) — citizen, fellow citizen (acc. pl. in -is = -ēs, with trepidōs)
cogi: cōgō, -ere, coēgī, coāctum — to drive together, force, compel (pres. pass. inf.; acc. + inf. after testātur)
commixtum: commisceō, -ēre, -miscuī, -mixtum — to mix together, blend (perf. pass. part., m. acc. sg., with clāmōrem)
concurrit: concurrō, -ere, -currī, -cursum — to run together, rush to one spot, throng (3rd sg. pres.; also perf.)
crimenque: crīmen, -inis (n.) — charge, blame; guilt, cause of guilt (acc. sg.) + -que 'and'
cuneum: cuneus, -ī (m.) — wedge; wedge-shaped battle formation (acc. sg.)
demissam: dēmittō, -ere, -mīsī, -missum — to send down, let down (perf. pass. part., f. acc. sg., agreeing with tē)
densaque: dēnsus, -a, -um — thick, close-packed, crowded (f. abl. sg., with mōle) + -que 'and'
descendam: dēscendō, -ere, -scendī, -scēnsum — to go down, descend (1st sg. fut.)
discindit: discindō, -ere, -scidī, -scissum — to tear apart, rend asunder (3rd sg. pres.)
drancis: Drancēs, -is (m.) — Drances, Latin noble, rival of Turnus (gen. sg., Greek form; Drancis dicta, 'Drances's words')
eruam: ēruō, -ere, -ruī, -rutum — to dig up, overthrow, raze (1st sg. fut.)
exscindine: exscindō (excindō), -ere, -scidī, -scissum — to tear down, destroy utterly (pres. pass. inf. exscindī) + -ne (interrog.)
exspectem: exspectō (expectō), -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to wait for, wait (1st sg. pres. subj., deliberative)
exstinctum: exstinguō (extinguō), -ere, -stīnxī, -stīnctum — to put out, quench; kill (perf. pass. part., m. acc. sg., agreeing with iuvenem)
fallis: fallō, -ere, fefellī, falsum — to deceive, cheat, elude (2nd sg. pres.)
frenum: frēnum, -ī (n.) — bridle, bit, curb; yoke of rule (acc. sg.; pl. frēna, frēnī)
immunem: immūnis, -e — free from duty, untouched, unscathed (+ gen.) (f. acc. sg., with urbem)
improviso: imprōvīsus, -a, -um — unforeseen, unexpected; improvīsō (abl. as adv.), unexpectedly, suddenly (n. abl. sg.)
incessi: incessō, -ere, -īvī — to attack, assail (pres. pass. inf. incessī, 'were being attacked'; acc. + inf. with muros)
indignus: indignus, -a, -um — unworthy (+ abl. or gen.) (m. nom. sg., with magnōrum avōrum)
inferior: īnferior, -ius — lower; inferior, less (compar. of īnferus; m./f. nom. sg., with numerō, 'less in number')
informis: informis, -e — shapeless, hideous, ugly (n. gen. sg., with lētī)
inlaetabile: inlaetābilis (illaetābilis), -e — joyless, unhappy, dismal (n. nom./acc. sg., with murmur)
istius: iste, ista, istud — that, that of yours, that (gen. sg., all genders; istius culpae)
laniata: laniō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to tear, mangle, lacerate (perf. pass. part. used as middle, f. nom. sg., with acc. genās)
libeat: libet (lubet), -ēre, libuit — it pleases, is agreeable (3rd sg. pres. subj., impers., with dum 'until')
magnisque: magnus, -a, -um — great, large, loud (m./n. abl. pl., with stridōribus) + -que 'and'
maioris: māior, -ius — greater, larger (compar. of magnus; f. gen. sg., with pugnae; also m./n. gen. sg.)
mittamus: mittō, -ere, mīsī, missum — to send, let go, hurl (1st pl. pres. subj., hortatory, 'let us send')
obumbrant: obumbrō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to overshadow, darken, cloud (3rd pl. pres.)
odor: odor, odōris (m.) — smell, odour, fumes (nom. sg.)
paucos: paucī, -ae, -a — few, a few (m. acc. pl., with palantīs)
perfusam: perfundō, -ere, -fūdī, -fūsum — to pour over, drench, smear (perf. pass. part., f. acc. sg., with canitiem; + abl.)
pergunt: pergō, -ere, perrēxī, perrēctum — to proceed, go on, set about (3rd pl. pres.; + inf.)
perpetiar: perpetior, -ī, -pessus sum — to endure to the end, suffer, put up with (1st sg. fut. of deponent)
quietam: quiētus, -a, -um — at rest, calm, undisturbed (f. acc. sg., with urbem)
recedes: recēdō, -ere, -cessī, -cessum — to go back, withdraw, retire (2nd sg. fut.)
reposcite: reposcō, -ere — to demand back, claim in return (pl. imper.)
reserare: reserō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to unbar, unlock, throw open (pres. inf.)
resonant: resonō, -āre, -āvī — to resound, echo back (3rd pl. pres.)
roseas: roseus, -a, -um — rosy, rose-coloured (f. acc. pl., with genās)
rutulas: Rutulus, -a, -um — of the Rutuli, Rutulian (f. acc. pl., with aciēs; Rutulī, Turnus's people)
spondet: spondeō, -ēre, spopondī, sponsum — to promise, pledge, guarantee (3rd sg. pres.)
stridoribus: strīdor, strīdōris (m.) — hiss, buzz, whirr, shrill noise (abl. pl.)
subitusque: subitus, -a, -um — sudden, unexpected (m. nom. sg., with ignis) + -que 'and'
subsistit: subsistō, -ere, -stitī — to halt, stand still, make a stand (3rd sg. pres.)
tumulumque: tumulus, -ī (m.) — mound, hillock, rising ground (acc. sg.) + -que 'and'
turbantur: turbō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to throw into confusion, disturb (3rd pl. pres. pass., 'are in uproar')
turbaret: turbō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to throw into confusion, disturb (3rd sg. impf. subj., purpose after ut)
turbasti: turbō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to throw into confusion, upset, break (2nd sg. perf. = turbāvistī)
turpans: turpō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to make foul, defile, disfigure (pres. part., m. nom. sg., with Latīnus)
vestigans: vestīgō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to track, trace, search out (pres. part., m. nom. sg.)
vestigavit: vestīgō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to track, trace, hunt out (3rd sg. perf.)
volare: volō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to fly, speed (pres. inf.; acc. + inf., ignīs ad tēcta volāre, 'fire flying to the roofs')
volgatur: volgō (vulgō), -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to spread abroad, make public (3rd sg. pres. pass.)
